target_customer: ASP.NET developers and small teams who wanted Heroku-style git push deployment for .NET apps
problem: Deploying .NET applications meant managing Windows servers or using Azure, which was slow and tied developers to Microsoft's stack. AppHarbor offered push to deploy with built-in unit testing.
business_model: Usage-based PaaS subscription with paid add-ons marketplace (Heroku-style pricing)

founders.name: Michael Friis
founders.background_notes: Quoted by TechCrunch on January 20, 2011 explaining the Azure comparison. No biography found.

exit.reason: The shutdown post gives no reason; it says the service closes after almost 12 years in business and hosting ends on December 5, 2022

competitors.name: Microsoft Azure
competitors.traction_then: Main rival per TechCrunch; AppHarbor claimed about 15 second deploys versus about 15 minutes on Azure

competitors.name: Meerkatalyst
competitors.what: Planned .NET PaaS addressing the same problem

competitors.name: Moncai
competitors.what: Planned .NET PaaS addressing the same problem

technical_complexity.rationale: Building git and Mercurial push, build, test and deploy pipelines on Windows hosting with multi-tenant isolation was a standard but non-trivial platform effort for a three-person team.

defensibility.rationale: Developers could move to Azure or other hosts with little change since the platform ran unmodified ASP.NET apps, so lock-in was deliberately low; the add-on ecosystem gave mild stickiness.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Microsoft Azure kept improving its developer experience; AppHarbor's own support staff later pointed customers to AWS Elastic Beanstalk or Azure at shutdown in November 2022.

market_need_then: Heroku had shown demand for push to deploy PaaS in Ruby, while .NET developers faced the heavier Azure deployment flow; TechCrunch called it Azure done right.

branding.domain_note: Used the exact appharbor.com domain; no purchase history found

identity.voice_and_tone: Developer-friendly, simple and fun per its own copy

branding.community_and_virality: Coverage by TechCrunch, SiliconANGLE and a ThoughtWorks Radar entry in March 2012; included on free-for-dev lists

brand_strength.rationale: Known within the .NET developer community and tracked by ThoughtWorks Radar, but no mascot or wider brand assets found.

outcome_analysis: AppHarbor launched in January 2011 as a Heroku for .NET and ran for almost 12 years, closing in December 2022 with only a thank you note and no stated reason. Its backers included Accel and Ignition per TechCrunch, but the platform faced Azure and later AWS offerings for the same .NET audience. The failure factors are inferences from that competitive position, because the company never explained the closure.
notes: The 1.4 million dollar seed with named investors comes from a TechCrunch page found in search whose publication date was not visible (it says raised last year, so likely 2012); only the search summary was read. CB Insights lists 20000 dollars from Y Combinator on 2011-01-27 and a 20000 total, which conflicts and rests on a single database. Company site redirected to the shutdown blog. Shutdown reason not public; failure factors are inferences.
